column2: Foundation: tenants, users, roles, permissions, channels, tenant separation, audit log, reporting views
Time model: work statuses, workdays, append-only time events with corrections, per-user time zones, identity lookup, reporting views
Corrections: correct_workday (also Add day), team_hours, team_day, CMA06, nothing before the start
Team people: team_people for Add day and the person filter
Tenant settings (catalog, tenant values, read and write functions), the workday.export permission and the export reads
Team status time: seconds per person per day per status for the Dashboard, needs performance.team
Clock in and app links: time_is_kept guard on day creation (open_workday, Add day), app_link table and app_links()
Team now: today's day and current status per person whose time is kept, for the Live board, needs monitoring.live

Teams and skills: team, team_member, skill, skill_level, user_skill; the admin role, users.manage split into users.manage_agents and users.manage_all; directory, add_person and the people and catalog functions

Roster: absence types, roster weeks with publications, versioned entries (shift or absence within the business day), coverage targets, the planner functions, the own schedule and today's shift reads, the adherence tolerance setting

Configuration: work status, app link, absence type and coverage target functions for tenant.configure; the scheduler system user and role per tenant with workday.close_forgotten; cma.close_forgotten_workdays() and the auto-close grace setting; a system end keeps a day flagged
My profile: cma.my_profile(), the acting person's own details, role, teams and skills for the My account page
Ingest and CRM records: connections with field mapping, pipelines and stages, the ingest log, thin CRM records and contacts with refs, the Ingest system user, crm_records_per_day

Intake core: markets with aliases, office hours and holidays, business time, connection settings and slots, CRM calls, call outcomes, associations, forms and submissions, sync cursors and runs, contact forget, people's ids in other systems
Telephony: calls with a stale guard on the source version, tags with history, lines with market, the keyed-hash call link to CRM calls, contact forget clearing linked telephony hashes

Commerce: stores (one per connection, unique handle), customers, orders with lines replaced as a set, order_kind (first, repeat, renewal, unknown) from the prior order count and the renewal settings, reclassified when a setting changes, the store in connection_config

Outbox and CRM contact write-back: write-back fields per CRM connection (always, if_empty, slot), the outbox with forward-only states, dedupe and supersede per contact, claim with SKIP LOCKED and backoff, parking after outbox.max_attempts and resolve by a person, outbox_status, the write-back fields in connection_config
Lead metrics and data quality: speed to lead with its summary, lead to order, intake per day, the data-quality checks, their reporting views

Messaging core and record alerts: messages, deliveries with delivered, read and acknowledged times, alert rules, record alerts for the ingest service, manual messages, the caller's reads and writes, stats
Assignment alerts (a record alerts the person its owner maps to, once per record and owner) and messages from automations through the ingest service (owners and emails as targets)

Workday window and forgotten-day close: window start and end per tenant (clock-in refused before the start, time counted up to the end, corrections within it), forgotten days closed at the planned shift end or the auto-close time with a notice to the person and a digest to management
Alert times in the tenant's time zone: the created and assigned time in the body of record and assignment alerts uses the tenant's zone, not the market's

Legacy time import: time_event source import with its batch, import batches staged, loaded and withdrawn as a unit, sessions, the person map and the days written; stage, load and void for tenant.configure; imported days closed by rule or clipped need a correction, a withdrawn day is no day; the batch key in the day history

Sources, markets and alert rules configuration reads, the connection kind, linked accounts on People (set_user_external_id follows the People rule); _owner and _user reserved for linked accounts; adapter names lower-case letters and digits

Uncounted lines: a telephony connection stores calls on its counted lines only; a call on a line that does not count is skipped, switching a line off removes its calls, taggings and links (ids only in the audit for those deletes)

Commerce phone hash: the keyed hash of the phone number on commerce customers and orders (the call hash's shape and pepper), accepted by the two upserts as phoneHash, cleared by a read without it and by a deletion; never the number

Commerce contact link: a store customer's matched CRM contact kept in the CMA (connection, contact id, matched_at), set or cleared by cma.set_commerce_customer_contact and forgotten with the CRM's privacy deletion; nothing written to the CRM

Inbound service and callbacks: the missed-reason catalog, three telephony settings, inbound service per day, market, line and hour, today's inbound with the calls waiting, missed calls not called back (the hash matched inside the tenant, never returned)

Calls overview and calls per agent: the connected-call threshold, calls, conversations, talk time and tag use per day, week, market and line with the previous period's totals like for like, the same per person with tags per person (no call id, hash or number returned)

Telephony history start: the business date of a tenant's earliest stored call (as cma.calls_of defines a call, in its line's zone, tenant-wide), so the Calls report shows no change against a period before it

Invitations by email: cma.invitation (the token's hash only, never in the audit), the two invitation settings, create, renew, revoke and list for the people rule, and the invitee's preview and acceptance, which bind the sign-in id when the verified address matches

Email activity, metadata only: inboxes and source channels with counted, market, work type and channel, classification rules, emails of two sources kept apart, inbox conversations and their events, the four email settings, the ingest writes, the market by email.market_order with the form step, the privacy deletions, the reporting views; contacts' country with fallback slots and its source, contacts held for emails and threads, the data-quality check contact_country_fallback

CRM tasks: the thin task mirror (ids, owner, status, type, priority, due and completed, the contact, deal and ticket by source id; never body or subject), the status and type catalogs per connection with is_done, is_callback and is_counted as configuration, the ingest upsert with the raw filter, the Sources read, contacts held for tasks and cleared by the privacy deletion, the reporting views

The follow-up layer: the four settings (ticket SLA in business minutes and its warning share, the age buckets of open leads, the callback window), the SLA per pipeline, open leads not called with their age bucket and last call, open tickets against their SLA, open tasks with their due state, the summary, per person and the person's own rows, the data-quality skip rule for unlinked outbound calls and the checks ticket_no_owner, ticket_no_market and crm_task_owner_unlinked, the reporting views

Forms reporting: forms polled apart from counted, form categories as configuration, the forms' fields with their options, choice answers only (checked against the options, filled by the backfill, never after a privacy deletion), the lead rule on Intake's form count, the market of a submission (form, market field, contact), submissions and answers per form and market per day or week with the previous period like for like, the history start, the data-quality check form_answer_not_in_options
